With all the good feedback for Watchfinder on Trustpilot I'm not comfortable writing this feedback but it's a true representation of my experience, upto this point, if things change I will reflect those changes accordinglyDuring a trip to London I popped into Watchfinder in the Royal Exchange in order to get a better feel for them after reading some not so good feedback elsewhere on the internet(reviewcenter). The staff in the shop were friendly, polite and helpful which gave me confidence I could go home and buy from Watchfinder over the phone once I'd checked watches for sale online. I part exchanged my 2001 steel/gold blue Rolex Submariner for a 2014 steel Rolex Submariner with ceramic bezel. First I had to send my watch in using Special Delivery with max £2500 insurance selected which covered less than half the value of the watch but took the risk, though I don't know if I would again, it was a relief when Watchfinder confirmed it's arrival next day. Watchfinder have been friendly, polite and understanding throughout this sale. After completing the sale I realised the pictures used on the Watchfinder website to advertise the watch I'd purchased showed black deposits in some of the engraved bezel markers, I highlighted this to the sales rep who sold me the watch he agree'd it wasn't right and promised it would be cleaned properly prior to dispatch. The dispatch team called me before dispatch to confirm my delivery address at which point I mentioned cleaning of the bezel engravings to be informed it had been cleaned and was now spotless.I waited in anticipation for delivery this morning when it did arrive it was well packaged.  Once unwrapped my enjoyment of receiving my prestige watch was somewhat diminished when I realised the bezel hadn't been cleaned properly as promised on two occasions, at this point I took a number of photo's and sent them to Watchfinder. To my absolute dismay Watchfinder suggested I send it back to them for refund, cleaning or a watch with a clean bezel which not only exposed me to £11+ postage cost more importantly it exposed me to being under insured if the watch was lost in transit, Watchfinder wrongly advised the uninsured £2750 would be covered by my house insurance. They are WRONG to say this as the majority of house insurance policies have endorsements for high risk high value items which say in the case of a watch it's only covered whilst being worn by you or at least in your person or deposited in the bank or at home in a safe meaning it won't be covered if lost in the post. With this in mind sending it back to Watchfinder isn't an option unless they provide full insurance cover which some watch retailers offer but Watchfinder don't.I purchased the 6mth old Rolex based on the description on the Watchfinder website and paid a price in anticipation of it arriving in as described condition. I have explained my concern over returning it partially insured but Watchfinder insist I return the watch to them under insured. As I write this I'm in a catch 22 situation I have to risk under insured postage and potentially lose £2750 if the watch is lost which isn't an option for me or try and clean it myself. I've previously owned 5 Rolex's and therefore I'm familiar with what to expect when purchasing a Rolex either new or used and how it should arrive. With Watchfinder what started as a 5 star Trustpilot experience has turned into this. At the end of the day I purchased an expensive watch from Watchfinder if Watchfinder said to me the watch bezel will have to be cleaned when I receive it I wouldn't have paid the price I paid for what was advertised as a clean watch or I wouldn't have bought it and gone for another or purchased elsewhere, unfortunately I found out after payment. What a shame a great experience ended like this.My advise to anyone thinking of buying from Watchfinder is firstly make sure the watch is as described though in my case I asked twice and it still arrived requiring cleaning, MORE IMPORTANTLY IF PART EXCHANGING A WATCH VIA THE POST MAKE SURE YOUR HOUSE INSURANCE COVERS IT WHILST IN THE POST I'M PRETTY SURE IT WON'T.RESPONSE TO WATCHFINDERS REPLY DATED 5/6/15Thank you for your reply, the general condition of the watch in question on arrival was good. The contaminated bezel engravings given the promises made that it would be cleaned properly is both unprofessional and unsatisfactory for an expensive 6mth old prestige watch of value £5000+. I base this comment on the 5 other new/used Rolex watch purchases I've made over the years.I take exception to being told how house insurance works. My watches are identified on my policy for cover home/away and accidental but as with the majority of policies items of value over aprox £5000 have endorsements applied like the following pasted from my policy:FG24. Jewellery ClauseSection 2 (Contents) and Section 5 (Valuables and Personal Possessions) excludes Theft and DIsappearance of specified jewellery unless the jewellery is either:(a) Being worn by you, or(b) Deposited in a bank, locked safe, or(c) Carried by hand under your personal supervision.I have serious reservations over the ethics around Watchfinder advising customers their house insurance will cover postal insurance short falls which is why I've advised they check the endorsements on their policy.I was fully aware that by posting my part ex watch I was taking a risk but appreciated that was my responsibility. Returning the defective watch because Watchfinder didn't clean it properly is Watchfinders responsibility.Yes you have given me three solutions all of which entail me returning the watch under insured. I buy and sell on Ebay and have experienced items being lost in the post and the postal insurance not covering item value, I'm not about to take the same risk with a £5000+ watch due to a fault of Watchfinders making.When I purchased this watch I did so knowing of the insurance issue should I have to return it but based on two promises from Watchfinder that the watch had been cleaned and my previous experiences with Rolex high quality I didn't anticipate having to return it. The fact of the matter is contrary to promises made by Watchfinder the watch wasn't cleaned properly and therefore through Watchfinder's fault I have to return the watch under insured which is neither my fault or the fault of Rolex quality.I live to far from Watchfinder in London for it to be cost effective or practical to return the watch in person as suggested. I happened to be in London on other business when I paid them a visit as I was passing through Bank underground station on return from Canary Warf. At this point I have no more planned visits to London.You've asked how I plan to proceed, as returning the watch under insured isn't an option I appear to have no option but to keep it and clean it myself once I find out how, the suggestion made by Watchfinder that I may be able to remove the contamination in the bezel engravings with a wooden toothpick is a little worrying as the engravings are highlighted with platinum and I don't know if this would cause damage. The price I purchased this watch for is £120 less than other online retailers are selling the same watch brand new with stickers for with the same offered for my watch I now wonder if paying the additional £120 would have been the better option. I decided Watchfinders 6mth old watch would be as described and therefore a good option. If the watch had arrived cleaned as promised I would have been delighted and left glowing 5 star feedback but it didn't arrive cleaned as promised. As trivial as a contaminated bezel may appear to Watchfinder we are talking about a prestige watch of value £5000+.FURTHER REPLY TO WATCHFINDERReference your reply I’m sorry you see things this way, to clarify matters it’s not a case of me being unprepared to resolve this matter amicably but more a case of protecting my interest. Your idea of what’s amicable and mine differ which is understandable as you have Watchfinder’s interests at heart and I have to look after myself.Watchfinder declined my suggestion I have the watch cleaned by Rolex at your cost which would have been an amicable solution alternatively another amicable solution is reduce the price I paid to reflect it not arriving in the condition advertised and I’ll sort out the cleaning. I’m as disappointed as you this sale has gone like this given my previous experiences of Rolex purchases.RESPONSEThankyou Natalie, as you aren't able to consider my options to resolve this mater amicably and as previous attempts to purchase courier fully insured delivery for a £5000+ watch under £100 proved a fruitless exercise, we'll leave it as is, thank you for your assistance in this matter.Under your terms and conditions for faulty items it says "Return postage, packaging and insurance will be your responsibility and you must follow our reasonable instructions. We recommend you use a tracked mail system and retain proof of postage. You must insure the Goods to their FULL value. You must ensure that you pack the Goods appropriately to prevent damage during transit". Your own terms and conditions suggest it's inappropriate to advise customers send faulty watches to you using under insured postal services assuming their house insurance covers the uninsured sum.Once again thankyou for your assistance.

After contacting them I have today received an email stating they are unable to locate a hard copy and have forwarded a pdf instead! I used the Watchfinder site to review details on pricing together with age and condition and after also reading information elsewhere on the internet settled on a Rolex Daytona based on its history and rarity. I agreed on Bluewater and attended the viewing. The watches were excellent, phone and email communications were excellent and I wouldnt hesitate to recommend Watchfinder.
